head: 25d21fe90e509d83c862a7c622d81a75ffd58c61
scope: One line of documentation: the resource table's Deployments row now reads 35 seconds instead of 30. No Go file, no golden and no test is in the diff, so nothing the earlier rounds proved can have moved, and none of it was re-run — the test for a number raised in one place and not searched for is the search.

implementerProof.how: The diff is that one line and nothing else (jj diff --stat: packages/envoy/infra/README.md, 1 insertion, 1 deletion). The number it now states is what the component renders — dispatch_kube.go:312 `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds: pulumi.Int(35)` and testdata/dispatch-pod.golden:177 `"terminationGracePeriodSeconds": 35` — and agrees with the same file's own paragraph at :213. The clause sits inside the app's clause, before the front door and listener clause, which is right: neither of those two pods renders a grace period at all (dispatch-tailnet-pod.golden and dispatch-listener-pod.golden carry no such field), so the row does not claim 35 for them.

proof.criterion: Review round 4's finding, and the class behind it: a number raised in one place must be raised everywhere that file — and the tree's live documentation — states it for this pod.
proof.surface: The tree at this head, searched rather than read: every mention of a grace period or of a bare 30 or 35 seconds in the operator file, then across the repository's documentation.
proof.command: jj diff -r b889f4f818b3 --stat; grep -n 'grace\|30-second\|35-second\|thirty\|stopGrace' packages/envoy/infra/README.md; grep -rn 'terminationGracePeriodSeconds\|termination grace period' --include=*.md --include=*.go --include=*.golden packages/envoy; grep -rn 'termination grace\|grace period' --include=*.md over the whole repository
proof.observed: Inside `## gcp:Dispatch` (README.md:122-277) exactly two places state this pod's grace period, :143 and :213, and both now say 35 with the same five-plus-thirty reason. The file's other seconds are not this pod's: :204 is the readiness window (`failureThreshold` 3 at `periodSeconds` 10, correctly thirty seconds), and :294, :297 and :410 are inside `## host:Listener` (from :278), a Docker container on a host with its own `stopTimeout`, health check and watchdog timer. Across packages/envoy the only places carrying this pod's number are dispatch_kube.go:312, the golden at :177, the pair assertion, and the two prose backlinks, all 35 or deriving from stopGrace. So the class is one row wide, not wider.
proof.negativeControl: The same searches do turn up one more '30 s' for this pod, and it is deliberately left: docs/plans/2026-10-14-dispatch-gcp-plan.md:98, which reads 'one Deployment of one replica, strategy Recreate, termination grace 30 s … containers envoy-dispatch, envoy-listener (Dispatch's ENVOY_URL is http://127.0.0.1:9020), the Tailscale container'. That is the whole pre-change arrangement this issue replaces, in a dated plan document — human-authored design history, which the repository's own guide says is not a Legion artifact. Editing it would falsify the history rather than fix a stale fact, so it stays; this is recorded here so the next reader of that line knows it was found and judged, not missed.

notRerun: The guard, the deletion and the rendering were proved in rounds 4 and 5 and cannot have moved under a documentation line: the guard driven in three directions (stopGrace at 45 s, at 30 s 500 ms, and the pod's grace lowered with its golden), the deleted inequality's cover proved by reproducing the regression it used to catch, and the per-object diff of all 35 rendered objects unchanged twice. The diff at this head touches one Markdown line, and envoy-infra-go and envoy-go are both success at this code head.

ciRead.runs: build, changes, envoy-e2e-local, envoy-go, envoy-go-race, envoy-infra-go, envoy-smoke, lint, pr-title, test and typecheck all success; dispatch-memory still in progress at the read; `dispatch` failure. No CI lane was re-run by the tester, and the tester ran no test this round: the round's subject is prose.
ciRead.redLaneNotThisChange: `dispatch` fails on the same single dashboard test as at the last four heads — `a cold Inbox hydrates every ask thread from its one list response` — which is dispatch://INFRA-76. This change touches one Markdown line; main carries the same failure, so a forward merge would not clear it, and the architect's standing instruction is not to touch it.
ciRead.consequence: It blocks arming, not this phase; the fix belongs to INFRA-76.

previousRounds.where: This file at c5a4ae303a65: the pre-stop wait charged to the server's shutdown, and a head id that was not a commit.
This file at 496d24b99d39: the guard fires in both directions and runs in envoy-go.
This file at 17d94f0d3255: the deletion costs no cover, the truncation case now fails, the ordering matches the Kubernetes documentation.

unproven: Unchanged since round 1 and still INFRA-63's: Tailscale Serve resolving the app's cluster DNS name under TS_USERSPACE=true; the cutover's two tailscaled processes against one state Secret, with the consuming program still minting the tailnet key Reusable: false; the front door's unmeasured 100m/128Mi reservation; and whether a release loses no request, which is what decides whether five seconds of pre-stop wait outlasts the propagation it runs alongside.
The reviewer's standing minor: 35 s is a floor rather than a cover, since the kubelet charges the hook's elapsed time — the sleep plus the CRI exec overhead — against the one grace period.
observations: The row now carries its reason as well as its number ('a five-second pre-stop wait and the thirty seconds envoy-dispatch's shutdown is built for'), so the next person to change either value meets the coupling in the operator table too, not only in the code and the guard.
scrubEvidence: Not applicable: this issue's acceptance criteria call for no environment or secret-scrub evidence, and this round changes one line of prose.
